The rule is real. It is recorded where cited, it rests on a real standard, and Tools' code puts most of it into effect. But no commit has ever met it, and the live public build was published around it.

WCAG 2.3.1 fails only content that flashes "more than three times in any one second period". So the 2.5 limit, the sensitivity runs, the second captures and the seed rules are Legal's own margin. What the code does:

- A clip above 2.0 and up to 3 needs a second capture, and the worse reading counts.
- A clip captured below 1 frame a second is void as starved.
- Any change to the player's content (render, sim, data, ui, audio, art) makes a pass stale, which covers camera, lighting, scenery, effects and crowd.
- A pass cannot be recorded without every required clip, so a per-change subset cannot count.
- tools/flash/pick-seeds.mjs picks 20 seeds and keeps the five worst from the previous release.

reviews.notes:
Verdict, in the auditor's terms: CONFIRMED as a gap, S2.

The rule is sound and honestly labelled. The 2.5 margin, the sensitivity runs and the seed rules are Legal's design margin on top of WCAG 2.3.1, not the standard itself, and the note says so. Neither the rule nor its basis is OVERSTATED or HALLUCINATED.

What matters is that the rule has never been met, and that the public /play/ build (pin 257a766c) goes around it. The owner-approved path in build-site.mjs reduces the pass to a report. The project's own readings for that pin exceed the gate: signature reduced 3/3/3, and per c623c1fa collapse 2/3.5/1. The live page admits scenes over the limit.

Why S2 rather than S1:
- The scenes measured over the limit are only just over WCAG's three (3 to 3.5 on the project's proxy, against the 5-25 Hz seizure range).
- A truthful click-through warning comes before anything plays.
- Reduce flashing is locked on.
- The page is noindex and unpromoted.

This state is acceptable only for a free, warned web build. It blocks any store release or promotion.

Aggravating:
- CI is dead, so neither a fixed pin nor the take-down can deploy.
- The site has no runtime expiry, so the 2026-11-15 owner date will not take the build down by itself.

Gaps in how the code enforces the rule's own text:
- The starved-machine check is only 'under 1 frame a second'. The machine's load is recorded but never judged.
- --verify does not check that 20 seeds were picked or that the five worst were kept; pick-seeds.mjs does that, but nothing checks its output.
- An owner record skips the red-flash and extra-seed checks.

Method note: WCAG says to analyse 'at the largest scale at which a user may view the content', but the clips are captured at 1024x768 or 960x540.

I could not reproduce any flash reading myself (no Godot or browser runs allowed). The readings are the project's own records, and only the live notice text was checked first-hand.

reviews.what_is_true:
The rules are real. The danger they guard against (flash-triggered seizures) is real at release. Their stated basis is WCAG 2.2 SC 2.3.1, and they state it correctly: a 10% relative-luminance step, three flashes a second, and the 341x256 window at 1024x768 (21,824 px). The red test is R/(R+G+B) >= 0.8 with a change over 0.2 in CIE 1976 u'v'. Where a rule is stricter than WCAG (c02 one event per 2 s, c04 two a second, w05 0.085 against 0.10, fx04 1.5 Hz), it is presented as a margin, not as the standard. One wording slip: fx05 calls the linear-value red test "the standard's own". WCAG does not say linear or gamma, and the analyser takes either reading, which is the conservative choice.

Status of each rule:

**In force in the code that ships, both the live pin 257a766c and HEAD:**
- The flash registry with the red refusal and a reduced budget of 1.0.
- The catastrophe light class: 120-tick gap, rise of at least 18 ticks, fall of at least 60 ticks, a calm form.
- The beam ripple at 1.1 Hz or slower, and the calm beam at 0.86 strength with a 0.3 s rise.
- Explosion flames that grow over three waves.
- The fx04 calm-mode marks at 1.5 Hz.
- The w05 facade budget, in the data and checked by city_check. I recomputed every tint's tone pairs, the sun-side fin included: the worst gap is 0.083, against 0.085. The inventory note that glass against a sun-side fin reads 0.14 is out of date.

**Written ahead of features that are not built, so no exposure now:**
- The sun and moon discs (w04) are scratch only and not in the sky shader.
- Magma (c03) and the exosphere bombardment (c04) have no effect built.
- The blast cloud is in the code, but nothing calls blastCloud.

**Not met:**
- The verification half. fx03 and fx05 say beams and explosions must be read in the release flash set, both modes, red flashes 0, before they ship. The live /play/ build serves beams and explosions with no recorded full-set pass: release-pass.json is for d3f1ca0e, and the pin runs under the owner interim. The live gate itself says some scenes go over the limit.
- effects_check tests only the core layer's lum_amp (0.04). The sheath layer's lum_amp is 0.16, above the 0.1 the check claims to enforce. Its sheath alpha is only 0.12, so the absolute effect is small.
- Bolts still draw a hollow muzzle ring per bolt, at most one every 4 ticks. fx08's letter asks for a steady muzzle light instead. The rings are small, under the area threshold, and not counted by the registry.

The header at movegen-banned.json:3 ("the build must fail if one slips through") covers the generator's strike rows only. Nothing makes these effect rows fail a build.

reviews.notes: The claim is true as stated (verdict CONFIRMED-MINOR). It is real in the public repo and the live /play/ build, but it causes no harm to players: it is not a seizure, code or data risk. The buff is a few percent. For RIVAL's menace to fill, the villain's own share of the 12-30% civilian toll (normalised to 425) has to be large, so a typical match likely gives about +1.5-3% damage and +0.3-0.6 ki/s. That figure is my estimate, not a measurement; I ran no batch. Most of the weight is that the build contradicts Orb's direct creative ruling (Pillar 5) and Legal's own c08 rule. That part is creative direction or team process, so as a safety item it is partly MISFILED. It is an internal consistency bug, not a legal exposure. Where it would bite is a store rating questionnaire. The rating there is driven mainly by the civilian toll itself; a mechanic that rewards those deaths can only push it up and must be disclosed honestly, so menace's inputs should be converted before any store submission. The fix RL-217 describes is to feed menace from evacuees, structures, wreckage and damage to fighters, and to let casualties feed only anguish as a cost. That change has to follow the pin-move rules because it changes fights. The claim also misses two more toll-linked benefits: casualties feed power, which raises tier (collateral.gd:358, fighter.gd:555), and at full menace, rising casualties stop the meter decaying (fighter.gd:699). Separately, RL-214 records that the villain AI's launch scoring prefers populated landings, which adds to the effect; I did not re-check that here. I wrote no evidence file and changed nothing in the repo.

The claim is true. I traced it in the committed code but did not reproduce it, because Godot runs are not allowed here. The net/*.gd files at HEAD match a8bc66e2, the commit the LAN folders were built from (git diff a8bc66e2 HEAD -- net/*.gd is empty).

(1) The handshake delay has no cap. NetHandshake.take does `theirs = int(pk.get("delay", -1))` and _agree sets `delay = maxi(int(mine.delay), theirs)`. NetDelay caps only this PC's own proposal, at maxDelay 8. NetHost._start passes hs.delay straight to NetSession.new. NetSession._init then runs `for t in range(delay): d[t] = NEUTRAL` for each player. A hello with a delay around 1e9 or larger makes the main thread fill a Dictionary until it freezes or runs out of memory. A smaller but still huge value leaves the match with input lag of hours, so it is effectively dead.

The version and match-key checks do not stop this. The honest peer puts its match key in every hello it sends, so the attacker just copies it.

(2) Kind-2 (Variant) packets go through bytes_to_var. decode returns any Dictionary. NetHost._take checks only the "hs" key and from == remote, then:
- loops over `pk.inputs` with no count limit, and the start tick `first` is the sender's own value. ENet's default maximum packet size is 32 MiB, and Godot's ENetConnection does not lower it, so one packet can carry about 4 million inputs.
- loops over `pk.ai`, calling session.takeover(int(tk[0]), int(tk[1])) with no slot check.
The inputs dictionary is never pruned, so repeated packets make memory grow without limit.

The takeover slot does less than the claim implies. It does not exhaust memory by itself. A slot equal to this PC's own slot hands the victim's fighter to the computer, which is a game-integrity problem. An out-of-range slot sets aiFrom[k] before inputs[k] is indexed, which causes script errors and leaves a bogus entry behind. Takeovers sent with ever-smaller ticks rescan every input key each time. Even the binary packet path, which caps counts at 255, lets a peer spray inputs at any u32 tick and pass any slot number up to 255.

Reach: only in the patched private LAN kit. The host binds its own LAN address on UDP 47100 and accepts the first peer on its /24. The PC that joins is just as exposed to a hostile host. It is not reachable from any public build or from /play/.

The claim is scoped correctly to the private LAN build, and its file and line pointers are accurate. The loop sits at session.gd:125-134, inside the cited range 110-176. By the auditor's rubric it is CONFIRMED-MINOR.

Likelihood is low. An attacker would need to be on Orb's home /24 while a test is running and connect before the friend does. Two other routes need a trusted person to turn hostile: the friend (Orb 2) attacking, or the host PC attacking the PC that joins. The harm is denial of service on a home PC: a freeze or out-of-memory crash of the game, and possibly memory pressure on the whole system. It is not code execution: bytes_to_var never builds objects.

Evidence strength: traced in code, not reproduced.

The takeover-slot part is mostly about game integrity: a peer can hand the victim's own fighter to the computer, or cause script errors. It is not a memory problem on its own.

Not reachable at public release: the desktop presets exclude net/, and nothing in the committed tree or the /play/ pin calls into net/. ENet is a native transport the browser build cannot use.

Online play after launch is planned. Before any netcode ships publicly, these must all be fixed, and at that point the issue would rise to S2 or worse:
- clamp the other peer's delay to NetDelay's maxDelay
- reject kind-2 packets that carry game fields, or validate their types and counts
- bound `first` to a window around the current frame
- allow a peer to take over only its own slot

The claim is accurate for the private LAN build. Both a8bc66e2 and HEAD have the same net/session.gd, host.gd, lan.gd and enet_transport.gd. NetSession stops stepping once it is maxAhead (20) ticks past the confirmed frontier. Since the remote's inputs arrive input-delay ticks ahead, the survivor's sim freezes about 20 to 22 ticks (roughly 0.35 s at 60 Hz) after the last packet. The kit swaps SimCore.step for lan.tick, so a stalled session means the sim does not advance while the frame keeps drawing.

The only notice is the window title, and it is weaker than the claim says. The title reads "The other PC has gone" only after ENet reports a disconnect or error. During a stall or crash, until ENet's own timeout fires (net/ never sets one), the title keeps saying "Connected, input wait N ticks" over a frozen match. There is no in-game HUD message. The window is windowed, so the title can be seen.

The AI takeover (proposeTakeover/dropSlot) is never called by any game code, only by net/tools/rollback_check.gd. The LAN kit also deliberately blocks toggle_ai in LAN builds. rollback.md:312 describes a host timeout that would call dropSlot, but no host does.

Scope: this is private-only. net/ did not exist at the public /play/ pin 257a766c. Main has no LAN hooks, because lan_kit.mjs patches them into a scratch copy. The desktop export presets exclude net/*. The kit's instructions tell players to close both windows when the title says "The other PC has gone".

reviews.notes:
My verdict: CONFIRMED-MINOR, and arguably MISFILED. It is a networking robustness and UX gap in a private test build, not a release-safety matter. There is no crash, data loss or player harm: the match just freezes and the players have to restart, which the kit's instructions already tell them to do. It cannot reach public players. Neither the public web build nor the desktop builds contain any net/ or LAN code, and online play is planned for after launch (CLAUDE.md). It belongs on Netcode's backlog as a precondition for any public online or LAN feature, where it would become S2: wire a host timeout to dropSlot, or show an in-game disconnect or stall notice.

One correction to the wording. "Only a window-title notice" is generous for stalls and crashes. Until ENet times out, the title keeps saying "Connected", so for those seconds there is no notice at all. A clean close of the other PC does send a disconnect.

Likelihood in private play: medium, since an old PC on home Wi-Fi can stall or drop. Evidence strength: traced in code, not reproduced (no Godot runs were allowed). I did not give a figure for Godot's default ENet timeout because I did not check a primary source for it.

reviews.what_is_true:
Every part of the claim about what the game shows is true. It holds in the committed tree (HEAD and the LAN commit a8bc66e2) and in the live /play/ pin 257a766c.

1. Pause screen and match-over card. ui/data/features.json has minimal_hud=true and civilian_bar=true. With those on, the pause menu feeds over_facts() into the card, so the pause screen shows "Civilians lost: n of total" plus buildings and craters at any moment of a fight. The match-over card shows the same lines.

2. F2. F2 is handled in render/core/main.gd _unhandled_input with no debug-build check, and the UI HUD does not consume it during play. It calls set_legacy_hud, which turns on the greybox HUD. That HUD draws a running "CIVILIANS LOST n / pop0" every frame and a MENACE bar on the villain's panel. The key list that names F2 is hidden by default (key_help off, --keyhelp only), so F2 is reachable but not advertised.

The part that is overstated is "against the project's own rule". The rule cited is the EP's decision (vision.md:1347; civilian-bar.md): no running number during the fight, and the exact count on the results screen. So:
- The match-over card count is what that rule asks for, not a breach.
- The pause-screen count was a documented, deliberate design choice (minimal-hud.md:31). It sits uneasily with "no running number", but it is not an accident.
- Only F2 is a clean breach of the cited rule.

Orb's later direction is stricter and does cover all three: "no death counters" (pillar 5, 2026-10-31) and RL-247, which retires "civilians lost" from anything players see. RL-247 puts any change in UI or strings on hold until Orb's follow-up, so the build is knowingly unchanged.

On release harm: Legal's own c08 analysis calls showing the toll as a count, with no reward, the acceptable way to depict it for ratings. That makes this mainly a mismatch between the build and Orb's and the EP's design rules, not harm to players.

reviews.notes:
Suggested verdict: OVERSTATED, leaning MISFILED.

Evidence strength is high: everything above is traced in committed code, both at HEAD and at the live pin 257a766c. I did not reproduce it in a running build, because no Godot or browser was allowed. Likelihood that a public player sees the counts: high for the pause screen and match-over card, which appear in normal play. Low for F2, which is undocumented to players (key help is off by default) but is one key press with no gate.

Why OVERSTATED: the claim says the pause and match-over counts go against the rule that no running civilian count is shown. The rule as the EP wrote it (vision.md:1347, civilian-bar.md:3 and :10) explicitly puts the exact count on the results screen. The pause-screen count was moved there on purpose by the minimal HUD (minimal-hud.md:31, which cites Legal c08). Only the F2 greybox HUD is a clear breach of the cited rule.

Orb's stricter direction does make all three contrary to the project's current intent: 'no death counters' (2026-10-31) and RL-247's retirement of 'civilians lost' for anything players see. But RL-247 itself holds any UI or string change until Orb's follow-up, so this is a known, deliberately frozen gap rather than an unnoticed violation.

Why MISFILED, and why S4: as a release-safety matter, harm to players is nil. Legal's c08 rating analysis treats a plain count with no reward as the acceptable depiction. The 'no running number' and 'no death counter' rules are Orb's and the EP's presentation and creative direction. This belongs in UI's queue and Orb's pending toll follow-up, and its natural fix is gating F2 and the greybox HUD out of exported builds.

Adjacent point the auditor may want to check separately: the menace meter still feeds on civilian casualties and gives the villain ki-regen and damage bonuses (RIVAL/meters.json; collateral.gd:353-358). That contradicts pillar 5's 'never on civilian deaths ... no mechanical buffs tied to killing bystanders'. It is a stronger rating-relevant 'reward' concern than the counts, though Legal's c08 accepted menace as a power meter rather than a score.
